body:
I managed to find the source of the issue. Here it is checked if there is already a relationalColumn with the the same name. And if there is, the referenceColumn gets overwritten despite having a different target, property alias and so on.


https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/src/metadata-builder/RelationJoinColumnBuilder.ts#L191
Can this be caused if you have ManyToOne and OneToMany both sides have @JoinColumns?
`JoinColumns` must be only from one side - the side which defines the join columns in the table (e.g. on ManyToOne side). Maybe this is what caused your issue.

> `JoinColumns` must be only from one side - the side which defines the join columns in the table (e.g. on ManyToOne side). Maybe this is what caused your issue.

ok so how do I get rid of the prefixes when I remove JoinColumns from one side?
and what if the problem is already on the ManyToOne side?

> ok so how do I get rid of the prefixes when I remove JoinColumns from one side?

prefixes can be only from one side.

> and what if the problem is already on the ManyToOne side?

investigate the source code.

> 

Well, I have, that resulted in this issue mainly :D I have two manyToOne relations on an entity that share the use of one column but target different entities.
If I remove the ManyToOne Joincolumn in favor of OneToMany then I have a problem with prefixes

@pleerock Same problem here, it's definitely a typeorm issue that should be solved. It's not an issue of JoinColumns from two sides, but if you use the same column for two separate relations.

Would be cool, if this could be fixed :)
This appears to be similar to the issue described in https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/issues/9814.

issue.title: fix: Multiple relations with same columns cause invalid SQL to be generated

### Description of change

In `RelationJoinColumnBuilder.collectColumns,` `relationalColumn` is used by reference and `referencedColumn` is overwritten.
Solution: Create a copy of the found `relationalColumn`.
